items.q: The science of the terms and rules used to judge hadith.
The chain of narrators of a hadith.
The text of a hadith, after the chain.
A hadith that is sound, the highest grade.
A hadith that is good, a little below sahih.
A hadith that is weak.
A fabricated report falsely called a hadith.
A report narrated by so many that they could not have agreed on a lie.
A report that does not reach the level of mutawatir.
A hadith in which Allah's words are narrated by our Beloved Prophet ﷺ in His ﷺ own wording, outside the Qur'an.
A narrator who is trustworthy and precise.
The science of praising and criticising narrators.
A narration that goes back to our Beloved Prophet ﷺ Himself ﷺ.
A narration that stops at a Companion.
A narration that stops at a Successor.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ warned that whoever lies about Him ﷺ on purpose should take his seat in the Fire (paraphrased). This hadith's grade by transmission.
The person who narrates a hadith is called this.
A scholar who has mastered hadith is called this.
The short poem on hadith terms by al-Bayquni رحمة الله عليه.
The short book on hadith terms by Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani رحمة الله عليه.
The number of conditions for a hadith to be sahih.
The condition that every narrator heard from the one before him.
The condition that every narrator is upright in religion.
The condition that every narrator is precise in memory or writing.
The two conditions of sahih that rule out hidden faults and odd reports.
A hadith narrated by a Successor straight from our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, leaving out the Companion.
A chain with a narrator missing somewhere in the middle.
A chain with two or more narrators missing in a row.
A chain with one or more narrators dropped at its start (the compiler's end).
An ahad report narrated by at least three at each level, short of tawatur.
An ahad report narrated by no fewer than two at each level.
A report narrated by only one at some level.
A weak hadith that rises because of supporting chains.
A hasan hadith that rises because of supporting chains.
A hadith where the narrator conceals a gap in the chain, as by saying "from" instead of "he told me".
The practice of hiding such a gap.
A hadith with words of a narrator mixed into the text.
A narrator accused of lying, whose hadith are dropped.
A hadith with an unbroken chain to our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The weak narrator's report that goes against a reliable narrator.
A report by a reliable narrator that goes against those more reliable.
A report with a hidden flaw that only experts can see.
A hadith whose chain or text has been switched around by mistake.
A hadith narrated in conflicting ways of equal strength.
A hadith where a word is changed in its dots.
A hadith where a word is changed in its shape or vowels.
A short chain with few narrators between the compiler and our Beloved Master ﷺ.
A long chain with more narrators.
A chain in which every narrator says the same words or does the same act.
The famous musalsal hadith on mercy that scholars read first to students.
A narrator who lived in both Jahiliyyah and Islam but did not meet our Beloved Prophet ﷺ as a believer.
A supporting chain for the same Companion.
A supporting report of the same meaning from a different Companion.
The study of searching for supporting chains.
Hadith of a narrator who mixed up his memory late in life.
The eight ways of receiving hadith include sama', the first, which means this.
The way of receiving where the student reads to the teacher.
The permission a teacher gives to narrate his books.
The way of receiving where the teacher hands over his written book.
The way of receiving through a letter from the teacher.
The most famous book of hadith terms, by Ibn al-Salah رحمة الله عليه (d. 643 AH / 1245 CE).
The first known book on hadith terms, by al-Ramahurmuzi رحمة الله عليه.
The book on hadith sciences by al-Hakim al-Naysaburi رحمة الله عليه.
The book on the rules of narration by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi رحمة الله عليه.
The poem in a thousand lines on hadith terms by al-'Iraqi رحمة الله عليه.
The commentary of al-Suyuti رحمة الله عليه on al-Nawawi's Taqrib.
Ibn Hajar's own commentary on his Nukhbat al-Fikar.
The commentary of al-Sakhawi رحمة الله عليه on the Alfiyyah of al-'Iraqi.
A Companion's statement about something only known by revelation takes this ruling.
The view of most scholars on all the Companions' reliability.
The highest level of praise for a narrator, such as "most reliable of people".
A hadith that al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrate from the same Companion.
A hadith that meets al-Bukhari's and Muslim's conditions but neither narrated it.
The category of hadith al-Tirmidhi often calls "hasan sahih".
items.a: Both hasan and sahih by different chains or views

items.q: A narrator whose name is known but whose state is not.
A narrator known by only one student.
Most scholars accept the narration of a truthful innovator on this condition.
items.a: He does not call others to his innovation

items.q: The rule for acting on a weak hadith in virtuous deeds, under conditions.
"Actions are by intentions" is mass-narrated later in its chain, but at its first levels it is this kind of report.
The number of ways of receiving hadith that Ibn al-Salah lists.
The book in which Imam al-Shafi'i رحمة الله عليه set conditions for accepting a mursal hadith.
The Imam who accepted the mursal of the senior Successors, in line with his school.
items.a: Imam Abu Hanifah رحمة الله عليه (and Malik)

items.q: The Successor whose mursal reports al-Shafi'i رحمة الله عليه especially accepted.
items.a: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib رحمة الله عليه

items.q: Tadlis where a narrator calls his teacher by an unknown name.
Tadlis where a weak narrator between two reliable ones is dropped.
The book by Ibn Hajar رحمة الله عليه listing narrators known for tadlis.
The book by al-Daraqutni رحمة الله عليه on the hidden flaws in hadith.
The book by al-Daraqutni رحمة الله عليه critiquing hadith in the two Sahihs.
Ibn Hajar رحمة الله عليه answered the critiques of al-Bukhari's narrators in this introduction to Fath al-Bari.
The science of narrators with similar names written alike but said differently.
The science of narrators with the same name and father's name who are different people.
The study of hadith that seem to contradict and how to reconcile them.
The book of Imam al-Shafi'i رحمة الله عليه on reconciling hadith.
The book of al-Tahawi رحمة الله عليه reconciling problematic hadith.
The study of the unusual words in hadith.
The famous dictionary of unusual hadith words by Ibn al-Athir رحمة الله عليه.
The term for when a student narrates from a teacher younger than himself.
The term for two peers narrating from each other.
Ibn Hajar's term in al-Taqrib for a narrator whose hadith is accepted only when supported.
The number of levels (tabaqat) of narrators in Ibn Hajar's Taqrib.
